findings.reason: the section's premise and its negative control both describe a defect the owner already fixed, so the node would be built against code that does not need it.
findings.text: §5 asks the first step to be "find which comparison the check makes today", and that check already exists: `_committed_scope` (called from `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2197`) reads each cited commit's diff against its own first parent, so a path the base commit changed is never in `cumulative.paths` unless the run itself cited it. §5's deliverable — "compare the run's own commits against its recorded base" — re-proposes the span diff its own docstring rejects as a diff "of a span, not of a run", and its negative control ("a comparison taken from the base's parent must charge the base's path") is unsatisfiable without adding the very bug `_committed_scope` exists to prevent. The live defect is elsewhere — a run that cites no commit, or that is charged the worktree shadow diff — and §5 does not look there

findings.reason: naming the owner turns three "somewhere in the promotion/dispatch path" nodes into three one-file edits and prevents a second implementation of record reading or of the scope comparison.
findings.text: census of the same type across the plan's unowned sections: §4 (promotion-path exemption) names no file, though the executable-gate check it would bypass is `_require_executable_gate_command` at `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:246` and the stored-record read it would use already exists as `recovery_review_delivery._delivered_review_record:464` with the review-role promotion already implemented in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:250`; §6 (printed command) names no file, though the composer is `_health_review_compose_command` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:809`; §5 names no file at all ("the one place the diff is taken")

findings.reason: the section as written would produce a printed command that still refuses when run, defeating its own done-when.
findings.text: §6 designs its command as "`--around <path>` for each", but `--around` is plan-only: the option is declared `click.option("--around", "around_plan")` at `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2389`, validated as a plan subject at `:2538` ("`--around PLAN`"), and a path is named by `--path` (`:2390`, multiple=True). A compose command emitted as `--around <path>` would be refused exactly as the plan-slug form it replaces, which is the failure §6 exists to remove

findings.reason: §2 explicitly promises it is "not a second predicate", but the predicate as it stands cannot answer the question the gate must ask, so the change lands in `review_coverage` (return per-sub-unit document state) or the plan is wrong about where it lands.
findings.text: §2 requires the gate to treat the document unit as owed "only when the document-level text that changed is text the node reads as its contract (the summary, decisions and gates)", but `review_coverage` returns the document as one unit: `_section_digests` folds decisions, gates and dependencies into a single `_document` digest (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:364`), and the coverage loop covers it only on an exact whole-digest match (`:931`). There is no sub-unit granularity to read, see below

findings.reason: the plan must state that `review_coverage` gains sub-unit document output, so the author does not implement a fork in the dispatch gate.
findings.text: the same defect's second site: if the gate instead recomputes the document's sub-digests itself it becomes the second coverage predicate §2 disclaims, and will drift from `_section_digests`/`_digest_state`

findings.reason: the section's test cannot demonstrate the rule it adds, so the node would ship a test that passes before and after the change.
findings.text: §3's done-when assumes the answered-finding rule is what makes a 1 % edit to an anchored section covered, and that removing the rule leaves the edit uncovered. The word-share rule already covers any section whose done-when paragraph is unchanged and whose `_edit_share` is under `plan_change_threshold`: `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:949-959` applies it to every section, so the first done-when case passes today with no answered-finding link, and §3's negative control ("with the answered-finding rule removed, the 1 % edit to s5 must read as uncovered") cannot fail. The discriminating fixture is a change the existing rule does not cover — a done-when edit, or a change `review_need` marks as required

findings.reason: the section must either name the field it replaces or state in its own text why the plan's whole debt and the write's own debt must both survive.
findings.text: §8 adds `uncovered_by_write` to the `edit_plan` answer (and the edit skill's step 10) without naming a field it retires or merges, or why nothing can be. `review_owed` stays as the plan's whole debt, so one write answer now carries two overlapping uncovered lists that a coordinator must learn to read differently; the supplied counts (public_definitions 2062, cli_options 407, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23) already carry this surface and §8 adds to it without accounting
